citation: Violi F, Loffredo L, Pignatelli P et al. (2015). Extra virgin olive oil use is associated with improved post-prandial blood glucose and LDL cholesterol in healthy subjects. Nutrition & Diabetes 5(7):e172.
protocol: Mediterranean-type lunch (pasta 100 g, chicken breast 150 g, salad 80 g, bread 80 g, apple 200 g; 894 kcal). Study 1: with vs without 10 g EVOO. Study 2 (one month later, same subjects): with 10 g EVOO vs 10 g corn oil, crossover 30 days apart. Blood before and 2 h after.

reports.where: Table 2: before and 2 h, EVOO vs corn oil, mg/dL

note: Paired-meal contrast, fat_type: same lunch with 10 g extra-virgin olive oil vs 10 g corn oil (MUFA vs PUFA). Small oil swap in a real meal with insulin, GIP and GLP-1 tabulated. Watch: only 0 and 2 h, the statistics section says means ± s.e. but the tables do not label the spread, and the meal macronutrient grams are only in the supplement.
